conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you've been having severe neck pain. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been getting worse over the last three days. It’s sharp and constant, especially when I move my neck. I’ve had flares like this before, but this one feels different.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Different how?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve got a headache and feel dizzy. The pain made me nauseous and I threw up once. I tried going home after the ER gave me two doses of IV pain medicine, but the car ride made it unbearable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned you have ankylosing spondylitis. Has this flare been triggered by anything, like trauma or a fall?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I might have tweaked my neck in the shower a few days ago—slipped and strained it, hit my knee. But no car accident or chiropractic visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We did a CT scan of your head and neck to rule out serious causes like a dissection or stroke. The results came back clear—no bleeding, blockage, or aneurysm.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good, right? But why do I feel so dizzy and nauseous then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Those symptoms can still happen with severe pain, especially with your condition. The scan shows no neurological cause, which is reassuring. We’ll focus on managing the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on prednisone before for flares. Can I restart that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you already received a dose in the ER. We’ll continue your home regimen—OxyContin, oxycodone as needed, and the prednisone taper. We also gave you a lidocaine patch earlier.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the pain now? Any nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A bit better. Still stiff and sore, but I haven’t felt sick since yesterday. Can I eat something?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll get you a regular diet. We tried ketorolac earlier, but you said it caused gas. Since you’re allergic to NSAIDs, we’ll avoid those. Ibuprofen is on hold—don’t restart it until you see your primary doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ve been using Advil at home more often. Should I stop?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, better to avoid it. Long-term use can cause stomach issues, especially with your history of GERD. We’ll stick to your current pain plan and monitor your symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well overnight. Your blood pressure and labs are stable. We’re discharging you today. Continue all your home meds except ibuprofen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the prednisone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, keep taking it as prescribed, but follow up with your PCP to discuss tapering it safely. Also, consider talking to your doctor about your mood—you mentioned feeling hopeless. An SSRI might help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been struggling. I’ll bring it up at my next visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Keep using your CPAP for sleep apnea, and your inhalers for asthma. Stay hydrated and try gentle movement as tolerated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will the dizziness come back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely, since it was likely tied to the pain flare. But if it returns, or if you develop weakness or vision changes, go to the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the anemia the lab mentioned?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your hemoglobin is slightly low, like before. Your PCP should monitor it over time to check for any underlying cause.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll follow up. Thanks for helping me through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and call your doctor if things worsen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a good day.
